How far apart in age are leaders and the people they lead?

The age of each country's current leader minus the median age of its population. A darker colour means a bigger gap. Hover or tap a country for details.

      How to read it

      The gap is the leader's age in years minus the median age of the population, which is the age at which half of its people are younger and half older. A gap of 50 means the leader is 50 years older than the typical citizen. Small countries that are hard to see are marked with a dot.

      Sources and caveats

      Median ages are the United Nations' 2026 estimates (World Population Prospects 2024), via Our World in Data. Leaders and birth dates are those from the main chart: every birth date was verified against two sources, and countries where the leader's birth date could not be established reliably (about 30, including North Korea, Oman and Guinea) are left out and shown in grey, as are countries without a clear national leader. Country borders come from Natural Earth, via the world-atlas dataset, and are simplified. Disputed and unrecognised territories such as Taiwan, Kosovo and Western Sahara are not part of the dataset and appear in grey.
